reason: The Claude CLI's ResultMessage.total_cost_usd is the running total of the whole CLI session, not the turn's cost: the CLI bundled with SDK 0.2.118 (Claude Code 2.1.209) fills it from its process-wide totalCostUSD counter, restores that counter from its config when it resumes a session, and zeroes it on a conversation reset; against a mock Messages API three identical turns reported 0.000105, 0.00021 and 0.000315. The ResultMessage usage token counts are per turn (10 in / 5 out each time; the CLI builds them per submitted message), so only the cost was wrong. ClaudeAgentSdkConnection recorded total_cost_usd as the turn's cost, so every Claude turn after the first over-charged and _record_harness_run_usage summed the running totals into the run's spent_usd (0.00063 instead of 0.000315 for three turns). The connection now keeps the last total it read as a baseline and records each turn's growth, as #490 does for Codex and #495 for Grok: a new CLI session starts at 0; a resumed one starts unknown, so its first turn's cost is None rather than invented; a total below the baseline means the counter restarted and counts from zero; every ResultMessage the connection reads (stopped-turn tails, turns the CLI ran on its own) moves the baseline so the next turn is not billed for them; and a #511 steered turn joined across two CLI turns records the growth across both. The usage event keeps the running total in payload.session_cost. tests/v3/test_claude_harness_turn_cost.py (7 tests, all fail on origin/main) drives the real ClaudeSDKClient over scripted CLI transports: per-turn deltas, a three-stage mission whose spent_usd equals the final total, a resumed session after a CLI exit, a dropping total, a steered turn, and a stopped/background turn before the prompt. The other node ids are the existing tests of the changed drain, steer and adapter-resume paths.
exclusions: No frontend tests: no ui/ change. No native tests: no Tauri or Rust change. No Playwright: area:core-api (the real-Core journey suite matched through harnesses.py) does not run a Claude CLI or read harness turn cost; the Python tests drive the connection and the runtime directly. test_claude_harness_turns.py, test_harness_leftovers.py, test_harness_adapters.py, test_harnesses.py, test_vendor_session_recreate.py, test_grok_acp_compliance.py, test_harness_stopped_turns.py and test_harness_connection_state.py were run locally in full and pass but are not selected beyond the node ids listed. No full suites.
